lines: Stereo mixer strip that adds its input to three stereo buses, blue, orange and red, carried together on one polyphonic cable from BUS IN to BUS OUT
Turns the input on and off with a fade; ctrl-click skips the fade, and a press held for 0.7 seconds auditions this strip and mutes every other Glue the Giant mixer strip in the patch
A rising edge past 1V turns the input on or off, with the same fade the ON button uses, except while an audition is running
The left channel of the input when R is patched; with R empty, every channel of the cable arriving here is summed and fed to both sides
The right channel of the input; patching here stops the L/M/P jack from being summed and fed to both sides
Sets the pan position of the input across the stereo field, by a constant-power law that leaves the centre at unity
Sets the level of the input sent to the blue stereo bus, scaled by the red LEVEL knob unless the menu is set to normal faders
Sets the level of the input sent to the orange stereo bus, scaled by the red LEVEL knob unless the menu is set to normal faders
Sets the level of the input sent to the red stereo bus, and the level the two VU meters show
Takes the three stereo buses from another module's BUS OUT; what arrives here reaches BUS OUT unchanged by anything on this strip
Carries the three stereo buses as six channels on one polyphonic cable, blue then orange then red, left before right, each the sum of what arrived at BUS IN and this strip's send into that bus

Note — nothing is heard from this module on its own: its only output is the polyphonic cable at BUS OUT, and that has to be carried on to a Bus Depot, whose MIX OUT jacks sum the three buses to stereo
Note — the two SEND knobs start at 0 and LEVEL starts at full, so a freshly placed strip feeds the red bus only until a SEND knob is raised
Note — holding any ON button for 0.7 seconds puts every Glue the Giant mixer strip in the patch into audition, this one heard and the rest muted; a single click on any of their ON buttons ends it
Menu — In — a slider under the Fade Automation heading setting how long the ON button takes to bring the input up, 26ms to 34 seconds
Menu — Out — a slider under the Fade Automation heading setting how long the ON button takes to take the input down, 26ms to 34 seconds
Menu — Preamps on L/M/P/R Inputs — multiplies the input before the pan and level knobs, choosing between No gain (default), 2x gain, 4x gain and 8x gain
Menu — Blue and Orange Levels — chooses Normal faders, leaving the two SEND knobs to work on their own, or Post red fader sends (default), which scales both of them by the LEVEL knob

Master fader and VU meters for a bus chain, summing the three stereo buses to a stereo mix out and passing them on separately at the master level
Turns the output on and off at the FADE IN and FADE OUT times; ctrl-click skips the fade, and a press held for 0.7 seconds auditions this Bus Depot and mutes every other one in the patch
Sets how long the ON button takes to bring the output up, 26ms to 34 seconds
Sets how long the ON button takes to take the output down, 26ms to 34 seconds
Sets the level of the aux input, which is added to the red stereo bus ahead of the master fader; fully clockwise is unity
Sets the level of all three stereo buses together, after which they are summed to MIX OUT
The left channel of the aux input when R is patched; with R empty, every channel of the cable arriving here is summed and fed to both sides of the red bus
The right channel of the aux input; patching here stops the L/M/P jack from being summed and fed to both sides
A rising edge past 1V turns the output on or off, with the same fade the ON button uses, except while an audition is running
Scales the MASTER LEVEL knob, silent at 0V and full at 10V; with nothing patched the jack reads 10V, so the knob alone sets the level
Sets the fade time in place of the FADE IN and FADE OUT knobs, 26ms at 0V rising to 34 seconds at 10V; the menu chooses whether it replaces the fade in, the fade out, or both
Takes the three stereo buses from another module's BUS OUT
Carries the three stereo buses on one polyphonic cable after the master level and the fade, kept separate, so a mix group can go on to another Bus Depot or to send effects

The right channels of all three stereo buses summed, after the master level and the fade

Note — holding any Bus Depot's ON button for 0.7 seconds puts every Bus Depot in the patch into audition, that one heard and the rest muted; a single click on any of their ON buttons ends it

Menu — Fade Speed Modulation — chooses which knob the fade CV replaces: Fade in and fade out (default), Fade in only, or Fade out only
Menu — Audition Modes — chooses Normal (default) or Always audition, which keeps this Bus Depot playing while another one is being auditioned
Three stereo send and return loops on a bus chain, one per bus, each with a sample delay for latency compensation and a stereo mix out of all three
Delays the blue stereo bus by 0 to 999 samples before it reaches the blue SEND jacks or BUS OUT, to line it up with a bus that has been through a latent effect
Delays the orange stereo bus by 0 to 999 samples before it reaches the orange SEND jacks or BUS OUT, to line it up with a bus that has been through a latent effect
Delays the red stereo bus by 0 to 999 samples before it reaches the red SEND jacks or BUS OUT, to line it up with a bus that has been through a latent effect
Switches the blue stereo bus into the sends and into BUS OUT, or out of them, over a 26ms fade; a press held for 0.7 seconds auditions the blue bus. Its RETURN jacks arrive either way
Switches the orange stereo bus into the sends and into BUS OUT, or out of them, over a 26ms fade; a press held for 0.7 seconds auditions the orange bus. Its RETURN jacks arrive either way
Switches the red stereo bus into the sends and into BUS OUT, or out of them, over a 26ms fade; a press held for 0.7 seconds auditions the red bus. Its RETURN jacks arrive either way

The right channel of the blue stereo bus, after its sample delay; patching either blue SEND jack takes the blue bus off BUS OUT, leaving the blue RETURN jacks to bring it back

Feeds the right channel of the blue stereo bus on BUS OUT, added to whatever the blue send is passing; it arrives whether or not the blue bus is switched on, so an effect tail can ring out

Carries the three stereo buses on one polyphonic cable: each bus as it comes back from its RETURN jacks, or straight through with its sample delay applied where that bus has no send patched
The left channels of all three stereo buses summed, after the sends and returns
The right channels of all three stereo buses summed, after the sends and returns
Note — this module does nothing until another Glue the Giant module's BUS OUT is patched into its BUS IN; that chain is what the sends, the returns and the sample delays work on
Note — holding one of the three bus buttons for 0.7 seconds auditions that bus and mutes the other two; holding a second adds it. A single click ends the audition, which reaches no other module
Merges up to six bus chains into one, adding the blue, orange and red stereo buses of each to the same bus on the others
Takes a bus chain from another module's BUS OUT; its three stereo buses are added to those of the other five inputs and sent to BUS OUT
Switches that bus chain into the merge or out of it over a 26ms fade; a press held for 0.7 seconds auditions that chain and mutes the other five
Carries the merged bus chain as six channels on one polyphonic cable, blue then orange then red, left before right

Note — holding one of the six buttons for 0.7 seconds auditions that chain and mutes the other five; holding a second adds it. A single click ends the audition, which reaches no other module
